latest_release.body:
# Version 4.0.0 (November 6, 2026) > [!IMPORTANT] > **Read the [MuJoCo 4.0 announcement](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions/3773)** for an overview of everything new since 3.0, the interactive showcase at [mujoco.org](https://mujoco.org), [MuJoCo Live](https://live.mujoco.org) browser demos, visual showcases, and maintainer Q&A. ## Significant new features 1. [`89daf8d19`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/commit/89daf8d19) Added the [speculative](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/XMLreference.html#option-flag-speculative) enable flag for [speculative contacts](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/computation/speculative.html) to prevent fast-moving convex geoms from tunneling through thin obstacles within a single timestep. On the right, one step of conservative advancement between two rotating boxes. See [model/speculative/](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/tree/main/model/speculative/) for examples.
2. Added elasto-plasticity, with stateful plastic deformation stored in `mjData.plastic` (`mjSTATE_PLASTIC`): - [`e140c026f`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/commit/e140c026f) Ideal elasto-plasticity for joint ([springyield](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/XMLreference.html#body-joint-springyield)) and tendon ([spatial](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/XMLreference.html#tendon-spatial-springyield), [fixed](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/XMLreference.html#tendon-fixed-springyield)) springs (left). - [`0c0f63b3f`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/commit/0c0f63b3f), [`c39fe6f02`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/commit/c39fe6f02), [`e3bd72742`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/commit/e3bd72742), [`7cb32488b`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/commit/7cb32488b) Continuum elasto-plasticity ([yield](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/XMLreference.html#flex-elasticity-yield)) for 2D and 3D [flexes](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/XMLreference.html#deformable-flex), with separate stretching and bending yield strains for 2D shells, volumetric-deviatoric (von Mises $J_2$) stretching and 2D shell bending return mapping (right). - See [model/plastic/](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/tree/main/model/plastic/) for examples.
3. [`abaf8d518`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/commit/abaf8d518) Split the Python distribution into `mujoco-core` (minimal bindings and C library depending only on `numpy`), `mujoco-studio` (Studio and Filament renderer bindings), and `mujoco` (default package installing both). When upgrading from a pre-split `mujoco` installation with `pip`, uninstall first (`pip uninstall -y mujoco && pip install mujoco`) or run `pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps mujoco mujoco-core mujoco-studio` after upgrading so `pip` does not remove files moved to `mujoco-core`. detail.readme_excerpt: **MuJoCo** stands for **Mu**lti-**Jo**int dynamics with **Co**ntact. It is a general purpose physics engine that aims to facilitate research and development in robotics, biomechanics, graphics and animation, machine learning, and other areas which demand fast and accurate simulation of articulated structures interacting with their environment. This repository is maintained by [Google DeepMind](https://www.deepmind.com/). MuJoCo has a C API and is intended for researchers and developers. The runtime simulation module is tuned to maximize performance and operates on low-level data structures that are preallocated by the built-in XML compiler. The library includes interactive visualization in native desktop windows and web browsers. MuJoCo further exposes a large number of utility functions for computing physics-related quantities. We also provide [Python bindings] and a plug-in for the [Unity] game engine. ## Documentation MuJoCo's documentation can be found at [mujoco.readthedocs.io]. Upcoming features due for the next release can be found in the [changelog] in the "latest" branch. ## Getting Started 1. **Try MuJoCo in your browser.** Visit [mujoco.org](https://mujoco.org) to explore MuJoCo on desktop or mobile with nothing to install, or open [live.mujoco.org](https://live.mujoco.org) to inspect and drag and drop your own models in the WebAssembly version of the [MuJoCo Studio] app (slower than native C, since it runs in WebAssembly). 2. **Run a viewer on your machine.** Follow the [Getting Started] guide in the documentation to download a prebuilt release and run the [MuJoCo Studio] app or the classic `simulate` viewer (shown in [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P83tKA1iz2Y)) on your machine. 3. **Explore our online IPython notebooks.** If you are a Python user, you might want to start with our tutorial notebooks running on Google Colab: - The **introductory** tutorial teaches MuJoCo basics: [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/main/python/tutorial.ipynb) - The **Model Editing** tutorial shows how to create and edit models procedur
